newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha moves sideways in listless trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha moves sideways in listless trade.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were largely unchanged in thin afternoon trade on Wednesday, traders said.
"There was only one firm buyer seen in the market, the rest were selling," one trader said.
The potential buyer -- a South Korean trading house -- has been almost sole firm bidder so far this week.
"Maybe if people feel more comfortable at the current crude level, we may see more buying. But I think people are very nervous to buy at these relatively high prices," he said.
Crude prices gained for the third consecutive business day in New York and London on Tuesday.
Open-spec naphtha was notionally quoted at $211.50/$212.00 per tonne for first-half October delivery. It was bought by a European trader at $211.75 on Tuesday.

The contango in near-term naphtha spreads remained unchanged, after having widened in late Tuesday trading. The half-month spread between first-half October and the second half of the month was indicated at about minus $1.50.
Fuel oil traders were said to be waiting for Indonesia's extra low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) allocation for August.
Indonesia's state-run oil firm Pertamina was likely to have at least 300,000 barrels of LSWR stocks to sell, traders said.
